skip_reason: Existing-move logistics / customer service only. Inbound call from a customer whose move was already booked for the next morning (arriving 8:45-9:15 at a Public Storage unit on West Fifth). Her three asks were all post-booking service items: what heads-up she would get on move morning, why a $75 transportation fee appeared on an already-booked job, and a change to the unload spot (park behind the building at 3504 Fleetwood Dr rather than the 3601 Manaca address on file). The rep spent the call rebooking the job from the North Austin to the South Austin branch to eliminate the trip fee, then waived the fee outright when the crew assignment broke, and logged the new unload spot. No quote, no pricing pitch, no booking attempt, and no sales conversation of any kind occurred. The 85-point sales scorecard does not apply, so no score was assigned.
top_strength: Strong service recovery on a fee dispute: rather than argue the $75 transportation fee, the rep investigated the root cause (an auto-booking had routed a South Austin customer to the North Austin branch because South Austin had no availability), tried to swap the job with another customer to fix it structurally, and when the crew assignment fell apart mid-call simply waived the fee. Customer ended the call saying the rep had 'been great and helpful.'
coaching_note: Not graded against the sales scorecard - this is an existing-move logistics call, not a sales call. Two process notes worth passing along outside of grading: the rep opened by giving her name as 'Jessica' but confirmed it as 'Jesa / Jesper with a J' when the customer asked at the end, so the intro name is worth checking; and she told the customer she would send an updated email confirming the waived fee and the new Fleetwood Dr unload spot, which is an open commitment that should be verified as sent. The auto-booking routing a customer to the wrong branch and generating an unearned trip fee is a systems issue, not a rep issue, and may be worth flagging if it recurs.
phone_presence_notes: Genuine warmth and transparency while multitasking ('let me just poke around while I got you on the phone', 'I have so many tabs open jees'), light humor about her own crews being 'the best of the best', and the customer volunteered unprompted that the rep had been great and helpful.
